pattern.crimePattern: a woman discovers that her "civil marriage" certificate was forged by the man who gave it to her, and that her savings are in his name, and kills him
pattern.notes: Fictional family and registry staff. Customary and civil marriage are presented respectfully; neither woman is caricatured. The forgery's flaw is shown, never how it was made.

ob.text: A landlady reports a man found dead in the sitting room of a rented house behind the main road in Embu town. Kinyua Mbogo (55), transport businessman. The door was open when she came up at 06:40.

facts.text: Kinyua Mbogo was found dead in the sitting room of a rented house in Embu town; the door was open at 06:40.
He lay on the sitting-room floor with one blow to the temple.
KSh 22,000 was still in his jacket.
A large steel thermos flask stands washed on the drying rack, with a fresh dent; its lid is missing.
Marriage certificate: Kinyua Mbogo and Doris Wawira, a serial number, signed "Registrar J. M. Nthiga".

reconstruction.text: Two years ago Kinyua "marries" Doris at what she believes is a civil ceremony, and gives her a certificate. He is already married under customary law. The certificate's serial belongs to another couple; its registrar had retired.
In January Doris puts KSh 600,000 of her savings into his fifth matatu. It is registered to him alone.
Tuesday. At the registry, to add him to her NHIF cover, she learns her marriage doesn't exist. The counter clerk tells her to go to the police.
Thursday, about 20:45, he comes to the house. She confronts him. He laughs: a customary wife outranks a paper one. She hits him with the heavy steel flask from the table.
About 22:00 Agatha, who begged the address from the driver, knocks once at a locked door and goes home ashamed. Doris washes the flask and calls her cousin at 23:40.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Doris and a warrant on the back kitchen. Detain her after the search; the cloth trace (12 h) and the certificate examination (10 h) come back inside her 24 hours.
